from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Conditional probability is probability given a condition.", "It shrinks the sample space to the condition.", "Example: knowing a card is red changes outcomes."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Conditional Probability", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        sample_space = Rectangle(width=4, height=4, color="#FFFFFF")
        event_a = Circle(radius=1.2, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.3)
        event_b = Circle(radius=1.2, color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # Position them
        self.place_in_area(sample_space, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(event_a, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(event_b, 'D4')
        
        intersection_rect = Intersection(event_a, event_b, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.6)
        label = Text("P(A and B)", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(sample_space), FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(event_a), FadeIn(event_b), FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(intersection_rect), FadeIn(label), FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining Independence", [
            "Independent events don't affect each other's outcomes.",
            "Condition B does not change probability of A.",
            "Example: coin flips and die rolls are independent."
        ])

        # Define objects
        # P(A|B) = P(A)
        formula = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = P(A)", font_size=36)
        
        # Event circles
        event_a = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.3)
        event_b = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24).move_to(event_a.get_center())
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24).move_to(event_b.get_center())
        
        group_a = VGroup(event_a, label_a)
        group_b = VGroup(event_b, label_b)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(group_a, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(group_b, "E5")
        self.play(FadeIn(group_a), FadeIn(group_b))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Just show the objects, they are already there
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bayes' Theorem reverses conditional probability direction.",
            "It calculates cause from observed effects.",
            "We update our belief with new evidence.",
            "The formula uses prior and evidence probabilities.",
            "It turns data into refined knowledge."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction to Bayes' Theorem", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        formula = MathTex(
            r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A) \cdot P(A)}{P(B)}"
        ).scale(1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B2")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color_by_tex("P(B|A)", "#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color_by_tex("P(A)", "#00FFFF"), 
                  formula.animate.set_color_by_tex("P(B)", "#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)
        self.play(FadeOut(formula), FadeOut(self.lecture))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The fox scenario illustrates Bayesian updating.",
            "Start with a prior belief about location.",
            "Incorporate rustling sounds as new evidence.",
            "Calculate the updated probability of the zone.",
            "Bayes' helps us reason with uncertain data."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application: The 'Smart Fox' Scenario", lecture_lines)
        
        fox = Dot(color="#FF8C00", radius=0.2)
        observation = Circle(color="#00FF00", radius=0.3)
        line = Line(start=fox.get_center(), end=observation.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(fox, 'C3')))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        # Prior is implicit in fox existence at C3
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(observation, 'D4')))
        self.play(Create(line.put_start_and_end_on(fox.get_center(), observation.get_center())))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        self.play(Indicate(fox))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Key Takeaway", [
            "Independence means paths never interact.",
            "Bayes' Theorem creates a feedback loop.",
            "Use both to master predictive probability."
        ])
        
        # Prepare visual elements
        path_group = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=BLUE),
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        loop = Circle(radius=0.7, color=YELLOW)
        loop_arrow = Arrow(UP, UP+0.01, color=YELLOW)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A)P(A)}{P(B)}", font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(path_group, 'B2', 'D5')
        self.play(Create(path_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeOut(path_group))
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(loop, loop_arrow), 'B3', 'D4')
        self.play(Create(loop), GrowArrow(loop_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(FadeOut(loop), FadeOut(loop_arrow))
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'D5')
        
        # Highlight term P(B|A)
        formula_highlight = MathTex(r"P(B|A)", font_size=36, color="#FF00FF")
        formula_highlight.move_to(formula.get_parts_by_tex(r"P(B|A)"))
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula.get_parts_by_tex(r"P(B|A)").copy(), formula_highlight))
        self.play(FadeIn(formula_highlight))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Probability

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly review P(A|B) using a visual Venn diagram. Define it as 'shrinking the universe': given B has happened, we only look at the slice of A that overlaps with B.
sections.example: A deck of cards: If we know a card is red (Condition B), what is the probability it is a Heart (Event A)? The sample space narrows from 52 to 26.

sections.title: Defining Independence
sections.content: Introduce independence: Events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Visually demonstrate this as two separate circles where the occurrence of one does not shift or scale the other.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (Event A) and rolling a die (Event B). The result of the coin flip does not change the probability distribution of the die faces.

sections.title: Introduction to Bayes' Theorem
sections.content: Introduce Bayes' Theorem as a method to 'reverse' conditional probability: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Use a tree diagram visual to show how we move from the cause (A) to the effect (B), then back to updating our belief about A given B.
sections.example: A medical device test: Given a positive test result (B), what is the actual probability of having the disease (A)?

sections.title: Practical Application: The 'Smart Fox' Scenario
sections.content: Apply the formula using a concrete story. Emphasize how Bayes' Theorem allows us to update our initial 'prior' belief with new 'evidence'.
sections.example: A fox is spotted in a forest. Prior: 10% chance it's in Zone A. Evidence: A rustling sound is heard (B). If the fox is in Zone A, there's a 50% chance of rustling; if not, only 5%. Calculate the updated probability of the fox being in Zone A.

sections.title: Synthesis & Key Takeaway
sections.content: Summarize that Independence simplifies probabilities (multiplication), while Bayes' Theorem adds complexity by requiring us to account for prior evidence and false positives.
sections.example: Visual comparison: Two separate paths for independent events vs. a single feedback loop for Bayesian inference.
